advances:
In the full central common-order support, both relevant cutting-line chords
are retained in \(\overline{Q_{jk}}\), including at polygonal
breakpoints.  Their convex hull gives the generic sharp necessary bound
\[
\Delta |Q_{jk}|
\ge \frac12\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}.
\]
The exact crossing identity \(c=|Q_{jk}|+|R_{jk}|\) converts this into a
trace-product constraint.  The \(k\ell\)-row separator is automatically
nondegenerate, and optimizing its accepted strict bulging inequality
gives a second, generally incomparable product constraint.  Combining
both with the accepted sharp \(A_0\)-chord inequalities leaves an explicit
nonempty algebraic region.  Thus these mechanisms do not close the full
central support.  The remaining issue is simultaneous realization or
exclusion of the three directional chord profiles, separator offsets,
and equality-case slopes in one common pair of polygons.

proof:
Since
\[
q_j+q_k+q_\ell=-(\delta+2),
\]
write
\[
X=q_j,\qquad Y=q_k,\qquad
q_\ell=-(\delta+2)-X-Y.
\tag{21}
\]
The four supported strict \(Q\)-chambers are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
Q_j&X<0,\ Y>0,\ X+Y<-(\delta+2),\\
Q_{jk}&X<0,\ Y<0,\ X+Y<-(\delta+2),\\
Q_N&X<0,\ Y<0,\ X+Y>-(\delta+2),\\
Q_{k\ell}&X>0,\ Y<0,\ X+Y>-(\delta+2).
\end{array}
\tag{22}
\]

We first determine the whole \(q_k=0\) section.  If a point of
\(A_2\cap\{Y=0\}\) had \(q_\ell<0\), move it slightly toward an
interior point of \(Q_j\).  When \(X\le0\), the resulting interior
points lie in the unsupported chamber \(Q_{j\ell}\); when \(X>0\),
they lie in the unsupported chamber \(Q_\ell\).  The strict sign
persists for a sufficiently small displacement, including the case
\(X=0\).  Hence every point of the section has
\[
Y=0,\qquad q_\ell\ge0,\qquad X<0,
\]
so the section lies in the closed ambient \(Q_{jk}\)-chamber.

On \(q_\ell=0\), equation (21) gives
\[
X+Y=-(\delta+2).
\]
If a section point had \(X>0\), moving it slightly toward an interior
point of \(Q_{jk}\) would enter the unsupported chamber \(Q_k\).  If it
had \(Y>0\), moving it slightly toward an interior point of \(Q_N\)
would enter the unsupported chamber \(Q_{j\ell}\).  Thus
\[
q_\ell=0,\qquad X\le0,\qquad Y\le0,
\]
so this section also lies in the closed ambient
\(Q_{jk}\)-chamber.

Positive area in \(Q_j,Q_{jk}\) puts interior points of \(A_2\) on
opposite sides of \(q_k=0\).  Positive area in \(Q_{jk},Q_N\) does the
same for \(q_\ell=0\).  Both lines therefore meet
\(\operatorname{int}A_2\).  The relative interior of each resulting
chord lies in \(\operatorname{int}A_2\).  At each such point, a small
ball meets the strict \(Q_{jk}\)-side of the relevant line; at the
unique possible intersection of two cutting lines, it meets the strict
\(Q_{jk}\)-wedge.  Thus the relative interiors, and then their
closures, belong to \(\overline{Q_{jk}}\).  Both chord lengths are
positive, and the polygonal chord-length function is continuous at both
levels.  Hence the one-sided traces equal the full chord lengths, even
when another projected vertex occurs at the active level.

Under the map
\[
v\longmapsto(U,V)=(-q_k(v),q_\ell(v)),
\]
the Jacobian magnitude is \(\Delta\).  Along \(q_k=0\), the absolute
derivative of \(q_\ell\) with respect to arclength is
\(\Delta/\|\nabla f_k\|\), and along \(q_\ell=0\), the absolute
derivative of \(-q_k\) is
\(\Delta/\|\nabla f_\ell\|\).  This proves (5), while coordinate area
equals \(\Delta g_0\).

Write the two axis intervals as
\[
D_{k\ell}\cap\{U=0\}
=\{0\}\times[v_0,v_1],
\qquad
D_{k\ell}\cap\{V=0\}
=[u_0,u_1]\times\{0\}.
\tag{23}
\]
All four endpoints are nonnegative, and (5) gives
\[
v_1-v_0=\lambda_{2k},\qquad
u_1-u_0=\lambda_{2\ell}.
\tag{24}
\]
Convexity puts the convex hull of the two intervals inside
\(D_{k\ell}\).  Its area is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac12(u_1v_1-u_0v_0)
=\frac12\bigl(&u_0(v_1-v_0)+v_0(u_1-u_0)\\
&+(u_1-u_0)(v_1-v_0)\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\]
which is at least
\(\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}/2\).  This proves (6), including
degenerate intervals.

Subtracting the \(\ell\)-crossing from the \(k\)-crossing in the support
(1) gives
\[
0=-c+g_0+y,
\]
which is the first identity in (7).  Subtracting the \(k\)-crossing
from the \(j\)-crossing gives the second.  Expanding \(W=0\) and using
the two identities gives (8).  The trace alternative in
`eddda25c734d34bc` gives
\(\lambda_{0i}\le\lambda_{2i}\), including equality with its separate
negative slope-sum condition.  Equations (6)-(7) now prove (9).

Compatibility supplies the \(k\ell\)-row separator from
`b431dbefa8a4aec7`.  Positive area of \(P_\ell\) gives a point of
\[
B_{k\ell}
=\{(p_k,-p_\ell):\overline{P_\ell}\}
\]
with both coordinates positive.  Each axis interval in (23) has
positive length.  If a separator coefficient vanished, a point of
\(B_{k\ell}\) with positive corresponding coordinate and a point on
the opposite axis of \(D_{k\ell}\) would violate the separator
inequality.  Both coefficients are therefore positive.

For any retained nondegenerate row, put
\[
C=|B_{rs}|,\qquad
\alpha=\frac{\chi_{rs}}{a_{rs}},\qquad
\beta=\frac{\chi_{rs}}{d_{rs}},\qquad
p=\lambda_{0r}\lambda_{0s}.
\]
The triangle containment and strict bulging inequality in
`b431dbefa8a4aec7` are
\[
C\le\frac{\alpha\beta}{2},
\qquad
C>\frac12(\alpha\lambda_{0r}+\beta\lambda_{0s}+p).
\tag{25}
\]
Thus \(\alpha\beta\ge2C\), and arithmetic-geometric mean gives
\[
\alpha\lambda_{0r}+\beta\lambda_{0s}
\ge2\sqrt{2Cp}.
\]
It follows that
\[
p+2\sqrt{2Cp}<2C.
\tag{26}
\]
Writing \(r=\sqrt{p/(2C)}\), inequality (26) becomes
\[
r^2+2r<1,
\]
so \(r<\sqrt2-1\) and
\[
p<2Cq_*.
\tag{27}
\]
For the \(k\ell\)-row, \(C=\Delta c\), proving (11).  The other row
areas are \(\Delta b,\Delta b\), which proves (12)-(13).

The sharp chord inequalities in `6a9cc7c11e208bba` are exactly (15).
Multiplying the relevant pairs in (15), then using (6), (7), and (13),
proves (16)-(18).

It remains to verify that these necessary inequalities do not close the
branch.  For (19),
\[
M=\frac{57}{2},\qquad m=6,\qquad\kappa=6,\qquad t=9.
\]
The three cap triples are
\[
(u_j,v_j,c_j)=(1,5,3),\qquad
(u_k,v_k,c_k)=(1,3,5),\qquad
(u_\ell,v_\ell,c_\ell)=(3,2,4).
\]
Thus all crossings equal \(t\), all cap areas are positive and proper,
the left tails are \(9,11,10\), and every right tail is strict.  Also
\(M\ge m\) and \(0<t<M\).  The weighted contributions are
\[
W_P=-42,\qquad W_Q=18,\qquad W_R=24,
\]
so \(W=0\).  Equations (7)-(8) hold exactly.

For (19)-(20),
\[
\eta_j=\eta_k=\sqrt{\frac{51}{2}}-1<5,
\qquad
\eta_\ell=\sqrt{\frac{165}{2}}-3<7.
\tag{28}
\]
Hence
\[
\lambda_{0j}\lambda_{0k}<\frac1{100},
\qquad
\lambda_{0j}\lambda_{0\ell}
=\lambda_{0k}\lambda_{0\ell}<\frac7{500}.
\tag{29}
\]
Since \(q_*>1/6\), as follows by squaring
\(\sqrt2<17/12\), inequalities (16)-(18) all have large strict slack.
The \(Q_{jk}\) hull bound has
\[
\frac12\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}
<\frac7{1000}<1=\Delta g_0.
\]

The unoptimized row inequalities are also numerically consistent.  For
a row with coordinate \(P\)-area \(C\) and trace product \(p>0\), choose
positive formal separator intercepts
\[
\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{2C\lambda_{0s}}{\lambda_{0r}}},
\qquad
\beta=\sqrt{\frac{2C\lambda_{0r}}{\lambda_{0s}}}.
\tag{30}
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\alpha\beta}{2}=C,\qquad
\Phi=\sqrt{2Cp}+\frac p2.
\tag{31}
\]
For the \(jk\)-row, (29) gives
\[
\Phi<\sqrt{\frac{49}{100}}+\frac1{200}<1.
\]
For the \(j\ell\)-row,
\[
\Phi<\sqrt{\frac{343}{500}}+\frac7{1000}<1,
\]
and for the \(k\ell\)-row,
\[
\Phi<\sqrt{\frac7{125}}+\frac7{1000}<1.
\]
The paired \(Q\)-cell areas are \(g=1,g=1,g_0=1\), respectively, while
the paired \(P\)-cell areas are \(49/2,49/2,2\).  Thus every recorded
area lower bound, triangle containment, and strict bulging inequality
has slack, even if the optimized inequality is imposed for all three
row labels.  Setting the trace pairs equal as in (20), and assigning a
strictly negative one-sided slope sum at each equality, also leaves all
these inequalities unchanged.

The data (19)-(31) are only an exact scalar and one-direction-at-a-time
profile calibration.  Accepted fact `6a9cc7c11e208bba` proves sharpness
for each individual chord profile, not simultaneous realization of the
three profiles in one polygon.  Likewise, (30) supplies consistent
separator ratios, not three separators arising from one common pair of
bodies.  This identifies the precise remaining gap and completes the
proof.
statement:
Use the common-plane and exact-cell convention of accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f`.  Let \(N=\{j,k,\ell\}\), put
\[
p_i=f_i-L_i,\qquad q_i=f_i+L_i,\qquad
\delta=-1-(L_j+L_k+L_\ell)>0,
\]
and let
\[
\Delta
=|\det(\nabla f_j,\nabla f_k)|
=|\det(\nabla f_j,\nabla f_\ell)|
=|\det(\nabla f_k,\nabla f_\ell)|>0.
\]
Assume the full central common-order support
\[
P_j,P_0,P_\ell,P_{k\ell},\qquad
Q_j,Q_{jk},Q_N,Q_{k\ell},\qquad
R_j,R_{jk},R_N,R_{k\ell},
\tag{1}
\]
with all twelve displayed cells of positive area and no other
positive-area cell.  Write their physical areas as
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 &j&0&\ell&k\ell\\ \hline
P&a&b&c&d
\end{array},
\qquad
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 &j&jk&N&k\ell\\ \hline
Q&e&g_0&g&s
\end{array},
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 &j&jk&N&k\ell\\ \hline
R&x&y&z&w .
\end{array}
\tag{2}
\]
Assume the crossings, tails, finite-interior conditions, and \(W=0\)
from accepted fact `a2a9387275a2c97c`, and assume that the crossings are
genuine lower crossings as in accepted fact `eddda25c734d34bc`.
Assume also \(M\ge m\) and \(0<t<M\), as required there and in accepted
fact `b431dbefa8a4aec7`.  Use the one-sided coordinate traces
\[
\lambda_{0i}=\Delta\rho_{0i}^+,\qquad
\lambda_{2i}=\Delta\rho_{2i}^- .
\tag{3}
\]

Then the two full sections of \(A_2\) on \(q_k=0\) and \(q_\ell=0\)
belong to \(\overline{Q_{jk}}\).  In the affine coordinates
\[
D_{k\ell}
=\{(-q_k(v),q_\ell(v)):v\in\overline{Q_{jk}}\}
\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2,
\tag{4}
\]
their images are the two coordinate-axis sections, and
\[
\mathcal H^1(D_{k\ell}\cap(\{0\}\times\mathbb R))
=\lambda_{2k},
\qquad
\mathcal H^1(D_{k\ell}\cap(\mathbb R\times\{0\}))
=\lambda_{2\ell}.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
\Delta g_0=|D_{k\ell}|
\ge\frac12\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}.
\tag{6}
\]
The exact scalar identities are
\[
c=g_0+y,\qquad
a+e+x=d+s+w,
\tag{7}
\]
\[
2b=5(g_0+y+d+s+w)+7(g+z).
\tag{8}
\]
In particular, the non-strict trace conclusion from
`eddda25c734d34bc` gives the exact chain
\[
\lambda_{0k}\lambda_{0\ell}
\le\lambda_{2k}\lambda_{2\ell}
\le2\Delta g_0
=2\Delta(c-y)
<2\Delta c.
\tag{9}
\]
No strict comparison between an \(A_0\)-trace and its \(A_2\)-trace is
used in (9).

The \(k\ell\)-row in accepted fact `b431dbefa8a4aec7` has retained
traces and every compatibility separator for that row is
nondegenerate.  Put
\[
q_*=(\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2.
\tag{10}
\]
Its strict bulging conclusion and triangle containment imply
\[
\lambda_{0k}\lambda_{0\ell}<2\Delta c\,q_*.
\tag{11}
\]
More generally, for any one of the three rows of
`b431dbefa8a4aec7` whose retained-trace and nondegenerate-separator
hypotheses hold, if its paired \(P\)-cell has physical area \(B\), then
\[
\lambda_{0r}\lambda_{0s}<2\Delta B\,q_*.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus (12) gives, for the three row labels when their hypotheses apply,
\[
\lambda_{0j}\lambda_{0k}<2\Delta b\,q_*,
\qquad
\lambda_{0j}\lambda_{0\ell}<2\Delta b\,q_*,
\qquad
\lambda_{0k}\lambda_{0\ell}<2\Delta c\,q_*.
\tag{13}
\]
Only the last inequality is asserted here to apply automatically by the
new \(Q_{jk}\) boundary argument.

Define
\[
\eta_j=\sqrt{a(a+b)}-a,\qquad
\eta_k=\sqrt{d(d+b)}-d,
\]
\[
\eta_\ell
=\sqrt{(c+d)(b+c+d)}-(c+d).
\tag{14}
\]
Accepted fact `6a9cc7c11e208bba` gives
\[
\lambda_{0i}\ge\frac{2\Delta}{\delta}\eta_i
\qquad(i=j,k,\ell).
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (6), (7), (11), and (15) yields the two necessary conditions
\[
2\Delta\eta_k\eta_\ell\le g_0\delta^2
=(c-y)\delta^2,
\tag{16}
\]
\[
2\Delta\eta_k\eta_\ell<cq_*\delta^2.
\tag{17}
\]
For either further row to which (12) applies, one additionally gets
\[
2\Delta\eta_j\eta_k<bq_*\delta^2,
\qquad
2\Delta\eta_j\eta_\ell<bq_*\delta^2,
\tag{18}
\]
respectively.

The exact scalar identities, canonical tails, finite-interior
conditions, (16)-(18), the unoptimized row inequalities, and even
non-strict trace equality are mutually consistent.  An exact scalar
calibration is
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
P&a&b&c&d\\ \hline
 &1&49/2&2&1
\end{array},
\quad
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
Q&e&g_0&g&s\\ \hline
 &3&1&1&1
\end{array},
\quad
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
R&x&y&z&w\\ \hline
 &1&1&1&3 .
\end{array}
\tag{19}
\]
Take
\[
\delta=100,\qquad\Delta=1,
\qquad
\lambda_{0i}=\lambda_{2i}=\frac{\eta_i}{50}.
\tag{20}
\]
For each equality in (20), the separate strict negative slope sum
required by `eddda25c734d34bc` may be set to \(-1\) in the scalar
profile data.  This calibration is not asserted to be a common convex
realization.  It proves that the listed scalar, trace-product, sharp
chord, separator-triangle, and bulging inequalities do not themselves
give a contradiction.  The unresolved condition is the joint
two-dimensional profile relation imposed by realizing all these data in
the same \(A_0,A_2\) and the same affine arrangement.

All boundary cases are literal.  The convex-hull formula behind (6)
remains valid for retained boundary sections when either axis interval
degenerates.  If \(g_0=0\), it forces the product of the two retained
boundary lengths to be zero.  If \(y=0\), the last
inequality obtained from (7) is non-strict.  If an \(A_0\)-trace is zero,
the sharp chord conclusion says that the corresponding cap area or
\(b\) is zero, so the product constraint is vacuous rather than
contradictory.  In the full support (1), \(b,c,d,y>0\), so the relevant
traces are positive and the final inequality in (9) is strict.  Cutting
lines and their endpoints have planar area zero throughout.
